result.topic_en: Draft passage, heavily struck through and revised, on how a continuous function of a complex variable can be shown geometrically as a mapping of one surface T over a plane A onto another surface S over a plane B, leading to the claim that an integral has a minimum for exactly one function.

methods.what: A continuous function of a complex variable is represented geometrically as a mapping of one surface onto another that is similar in its smallest parts (conformal mapping).
methods.quote:

aufgefaßt werden kann.

methods.what: Minimum principle (Dirichlet principle): the integral, when varied over continuous or piecewise discontinuous functions, attains its minimum for exactly one function.
methods.quote:
während das Integral bei Änderung {+von λ [?]+} um stetige oder
doch nur in einzelnen Punkten unstetige Functionen [-erhält-], immer für eine und
nur für eine dieser Functionen ein Minimum.

items.english: We restrict ourselves here to considering the application of our theorems to functions in a more general case, where the function of a complex variable depends on an arbitrary function.

items.quote:
So [-bleibt für den Werth-] {+erhält+}, während das Integral bei Änderung {+von λ [?]+} um stetige oder

items.english: Thus, when the integral is varied (with respect to λ) by continuous functions, or by functions discontinuous only at isolated points, it always attains a minimum for one and only one of these functions.
